cases.served_question: In your own words, what happens from the moment someone uses your idea until it produces the result you want? Describe the main physical steps you expect, even if you do not know their technical names.
cases.original_idea: A pedal at the base of the toilet lets a person raise the seat with their foot instead of touching it. When the pedal is pressed, the seat lifts up, and when the foot is released, the seat lowers gently. The kit clips onto most standard toilets without tools. The goal is to keep hands away from a surface many people find unhygienic.
cases.preceding_answer: When the foot presses the pedal down, a steel cable running up the side of the bowl is pulled downward. At the top, the cable wraps around a small pulley fixed to the seat's hinge pin, so pulling it turns the pin and swings the seat up to about 90 degrees. A coil spring under the pedal pushes it back up when the foot is lifted, and the cable goes slack.
cases.current_answer: As the seat swings up, an oil-filled rotary damper mounted beside the hinge pin is wound against its resistance. When the foot comes off the pedal, the seat's weight drives the damper backward, so the seat takes about three seconds to settle instead of dropping. A rubber stop on the floor plate halts the pedal at the bottom of its travel, which is exactly where the seat reaches upright.

cases.original_idea: A pedal at the base of the toilet lets a person raise the seat with their foot instead of touching it. When the pedal is pressed, the seat lifts up, and when the foot is released, the seat lowers gently. The kit clips onto most standard toilets without tools. The goal is to keep hands away from a surface many people find unhygienic.
cases.preceding_answer: When the foot presses the pedal down, a steel cable running up the side of the bowl is pulled downward. A coil spring under the pedal pushes it back up when the foot is lifted, and the cable goes slack.

cases.served_question: Which parts do you expect to move or connect, and what does each one do to the next part? If you are unsure how force is transferred, describe the movement or effect you expect.
cases.original_idea: A small clip-on device slides over the flat sealed end of a toothpaste tube and rolls the tube up as it is used. The user turns a key on the side a little before each brushing, and the tube is squeezed from the bottom so the paste moves toward the cap. The roll cannot loosen by itself, so the tube stays tight. The aim is to use the last of the paste without waste.
cases.preceding_answer: The key is fixed to a slotted spindle, and the flat end of the tube is slid into the slot. Turning the key rotates the spindle, which winds the tube around itself. A toothed ratchet wheel on the spindle meets a spring-loaded pawl in the frame, so the spindle can turn only in the winding direction.
cases.current_answer: In front of the spindle there is a pair of nylon pressure rollers held in slots in the side plates. Two leaf springs push these rollers against the wound tube, so as the spindle turns, the rollers flatten the tube onto the roll and drive the paste forward instead of leaving it in the folds. As the roll gets thicker, the rollers slide back along their slots against the springs.

cases.original_idea: A holder that sits on a table and keeps a paperback or textbook open at the right page without the reader holding it. cases.preceding_answer: It needs a tilted base board that the back of the book rests against, held at about 30 degrees by a fold-out strut at the back. A ledge along the bottom of the board stops the book from sliding down.
cases.current_answer: Each arm ends in a clear acrylic roller wheel about 2 cm across, which rolls along the page instead of pressing on one fixed point. Its job is to let the reader slide a page underneath without lifting the arm. Each arm also has a sliding collar so its length can be set between 8 and 15 cm to suit narrow or wide books.

cases.served_question: Explain in everyday words how you imagine the system would notice the problem and respond.
cases.original_idea: A household power strip that watches each of its sockets for a plug that is getting dangerously hot, for example because the plug is loose or damaged. If one socket overheats, the strip switches off only that socket and leaves the others working. A light next to the socket shows which one was cut. The aim is to stop small faults from turning into fires behind furniture.
cases.preceding_answer: Each socket has a small temperature sensor, a thermistor, pressed against the metal contacts that grip the plug pins. A microcontroller reads all the sensors once a second, and if any of them is above 70 degrees Celsius it opens the relay that feeds that socket. The red light beside that socket then turns on.
cases.current_answer: Besides the fixed 70 degree limit, the controller also watches how fast each temperature is rising. If a socket warms by more than 10 degrees within one minute, it cuts that socket even before it reaches the limit. After a cut, the relay stays open until the user presses a reset button beside the socket, and the reset is ignored while that socket still reads above 45 degrees.

cases.original_idea: مشترك كهربائي منزلي يراقب كل مقبس من مقابسه بحثاً عن قابس تزداد حرارته إلى حد خطير، كأن يكون القابس مرتخياً أو تالفاً. فإذا ارتفعت حرارة أحد المقابس، يفصل المشترك ذلك المقبس وحده ويُبقي المقابس الأخرى تعمل. ويبيّن ضوء بجوار المقبس أيّها فُصل. والهدف منع الأعطال الصغيرة من التحوّل إلى حرائق خلف الأثاث.
cases.preceding_answer: في كل مقبس حسّاس حرارة صغير من نوع المقاومة الحرارية، مضغوط على الملامسات المعدنية التي تمسك أسنان القابس. ويقرأ متحكّم دقيق جميع الحسّاسات مرة كل ثانية، فإذا تجاوزت قراءة أيٍّ منها سبعين درجة مئوية فتح المرحّل الذي يغذّي ذلك المقبس. ثم يُضاء الضوء الأحمر المجاور لذلك المقبس.
cases.current_answer: إلى جانب الحد الثابت البالغ سبعين درجة، يراقب المتحكّم أيضاً سرعة ارتفاع حرارة كل مقبس. فإذا ارتفعت حرارة مقبس بأكثر من عشر درجات خلال دقيقة واحدة، فصله حتى قبل بلوغ الحد. وبعد الفصل يبقى المرحّل مفتوحاً إلى أن يضغط المستخدم زرّ إعادة التشغيل بجوار المقبس، ويُتجاهَل هذا الزر ما دامت حرارة المقبس فوق خمس وأربعين درجة.

cases.served_question: Explain in everyday words how you imagine the system would notice the problem and respond.
cases.original_idea: A household power strip that watches each of its sockets for a plug that is getting dangerously hot, for example because the plug is loose or damaged. If one socket overheats, the strip switches off only that socket and leaves the others working. A light next to the socket shows which one was cut. The aim is to stop small faults from turning into fires behind furniture.
cases.preceding_answer: Each socket has a small temperature sensor, a thermistor, pressed against the metal contacts that grip the plug pins. cases.served_question: What are the main parts of your idea, in your own words, and what does each part do?
cases.original_idea: A small clip worn on the back of a shirt collar that reminds the wearer to sit or stand up straight. When the wearer slouches for more than a short while, the clip gives a gentle buzz. It recharges overnight and lasts a full working day. The aim is to help office workers and students build better posture habits without anyone having to nag them.
cases.preceding_answer: Inside the clip there is a three-axis accelerometer that measures how far the upper back is tilted. A low-power microcontroller compares that tilt with a reference angle, which the wearer saves by double-tapping the clip while sitting straight. A coin-shaped vibration motor makes the buzz when the tilt is more than 15 degrees past the reference for 30 seconds.
cases.current_answer: Power comes from a 120 mAh lithium-polymer cell, which is charged through two gold-plated spring pins on the back that touch a small magnetic dock. A Bluetooth Low Energy radio sends the day's count of slouch buzzes to a phone app, so the wearer can see whether the count is falling week by week.

cases.original_idea: A small unit mounted on the inside of the front door that notices when the deadbolt has been left unlocked late in the evening. cases.preceding_answer: A small magnet glued to the deadbolt's thumb-turn is detected by a Hall-effect sensor in the unit, so the unit knows whether the bolt is turned to locked. A reed switch on the door frame tells it the door is closed. If at 22:30 the door is closed but the bolt is not locked, the unit's Wi-Fi module sends a push notification through the home router to the phones.
cases.current_answer: If nobody locks the door within 10 minutes of the first notification, the unit sends a second alert marked urgent, which overrides the phones' silent mode. At the same moment a small piezo buzzer inside the unit plays a short chime, so anyone still awake near the hallway hears it.
